To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the habituation of the human eye blink reflex is a complex process involving both central habituation and efferent sensitization, and that the relative contributions of these two components to the overall habituation process are determined by the interstimulus interval between the stimuli.
habituation and sensitization can occur within the same reflex response, and that they may occur in different components of a reflex response.
the human eyeblink response is a two-component reflex, and that habituation and sensitization occur independently in its two components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the human blink reflex.
the study of the mechanisms of habituation of the human eye blink reflex.
the effects of habituation and sensitization on the human blink reflex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sensitization is an increase in the amplitude of a reflex response to repeated stimulation, and that habituation is a decrease in the amplitude of the response.
the human eyeblink is a reflex which is composed of at least two components, R1 and R2, and that these components are subject to different forms of plasticity.
habituation and sensitization can occur within the same reflex, and that they are not mutually exclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain stem reflex pathway, as well as the peripheral reflex pathway, is capable of habituating to repeated stimulation.
, for the human eyeblink response, sensitization and habituation are independent processes.

the brain stem eyeblink reflex can be modulated by afferent stimulation in a complex manner, and the effects of such stimulation can be studied in humans by the use of electromyographic recording techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the brainstem reflexes that underlie eyeblink conditioning can be sensitized by a conditioning procedure, and that sensitization is enhanced when the conditioning stimulus is paired with a strong unconditioned stimulus.
the brain stem reflex pathways that mediate habituation and sensitization are different and that these pathways can be differentially affected by pharmacological manipulations.
habituation is a general property of the central nervous system and that sensitization is the rule rather than the exception in the efferents to the muscles.
